items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We were all on time for the session except Art... Art finally arrived about 4... Art claimed that he had had another recording date that he thought would be finished in time for him to do the one with me.

ctx.x: We were all on time for the session except Art. The starting time was two o'clock in the afternoon. So while waiting for Art, Jean Pierre Sasson and I composed a number and called it "Jumping at Pleyel" because we were recording on the stage of the Salle Pleyel. We recorded this number with the rhythm session minus piano and the other instruments.

Art finally arrived about 4, and naturally Canetti and none of the rest of us were happy about this. Art claimed that he had had another recording date that he thought would be finished in time for him to do the one with me. Canetti said that he never would use Art for another session and Boucaya who was doing a lot of studio work said that something like that only happens with jazz musicians.....

One night in November, I was surprised to see Josh White, the popular folk singer and guitarist come into the club. When we had a break, I went to his table. He was with some English people and he had come to Paris from London where he was working, to do a radio show for B.B.C. He engaged me and the band to do his show which was to be heard at Christmas and we recorded it the 23rd of November.
